# The three-spoke Boolean cube has a two-W-block conservation law; singleton fibers are endpoint attachments

**Workspace:** D17
**State:** established
**Key:** `three-spoke-boolean-cube-block-conservation`

**Summary:** In the Boolean exact-two-cover cube G_J=W∪J generated by a three-spoke source frame, fix the common Hamilton five-set K={a,c,p,q,r}. For every nonempty J⊆{p,q,r} and every exact two-cover T_J of G_J, R560 applied with absorber K and overlap J forces at least two maximal W-blocks. If there are at least three, those blocks give a ≥3-cover of W against its exact two-cover, so R159 fires on the common core. Otherwise there are exactly two W-blocks. Contracting them in the two-rail forest gives the exact identity p_J+tau_J=|J|, where p_J counts selected J-J states and tau_J selected J-W transitions. Hence every singleton quiet fiber W+s has tau=1: s is literally a rail endpoint attached to one W-block, and trimming s gives an exact two-cover of W. For |J|=2 the only quiet cells are (p,tau)=(1,1),(0,2); for the top fiber p+tau=3. Comparing the three singleton trims by R471 further reduces the no-disagreement branch to three endpoint attachments over one common literal two-cover of W. This is a static finite normal form, not absorption: R159/R435 outputs remain constructive data and the common-base endpoint trident still needs a direct two-cover consumer.

### 1. Setup from the order-uniform three-spoke cube
Retain a hypothetical smallest counterexample H, one exact source frame H-{a,c}=U|V, and three distinct internal same-orientation spokes

  P={p,q,r},
  (a,s,c) tight for every s in P.

Put

  K={a,c,p,q,r},
  W=V(H)-K,
  G_J=H[W union J] for J subseteq P.

Retain the Boolean-cube conclusions of SV96081: K is Hamiltonian; every G_J is non-Hamiltonian with pc(G_J)=2; in particular W has an exact two-cover.

### 2. R560 forces at least two W-blocks in every nonempty fiber
Fix nonempty J subseteq P and an arbitrary literal exact two-cover

  T_J=T_1|T_2

of G_J. Apply R560 with

  D=K-J,
  S=J,
  C=W,
  A=K.

Here A is one Hamilton path on D union S=K and T_J is a two-cover of H-D=G_J. Since pc(H)=3, R560 gives

  b_W(T_J)>=2,                                      (BCB.1)

where b_W(T_J) is the number of maximal nonempty W-blocks in the two displayed rails.

If b_W(T_J)>=3, delete the J-vertices and split at every former J|W transition. The surviving maximal W-blocks are literal tight paths covering exactly W, so they give a b_W(T_J)-cover of W. Since W also has an exact two-cover, accepted R159 applies on the proper subsystem W and yields its graph-intrinsic component-drop balanced-pair output.

Thus outside that common-W component-drop output,

  b_W(T_J)=2.                                        (BCB.2)

For J=emptyset the same equality is automatic because an exact two-cover of W consists of exactly two maximal W-blocks.

### 3. Exact conservation after contracting the two W-blocks
Assume (BCB.2). Contract each of the two maximal W-blocks of T_J to one vertex and leave every spoke of J as its own vertex. Contraction preserves the number of path components, so the result is a forest with

  |J|+2 vertices and exactly two path components.

Hence it has exactly |J| selected edges. No edge joins the two distinct W-block vertices, because they were maximal W-blocks. Every contracted selected edge is therefore either

- a selected J-J state, or
- a selected J-W transition.

Let p_J count the former and tau_J the latter. Then

  p_J + tau_J = |J|.                                (BCB.3)

This identity is representative-relative to T_J but otherwise exact.

### 4. Singleton fibers are literal endpoint attachments
Take J={s}. Then p_J=0, so (BCB.3) gives

  tau_J=1.

Equivalently, every exact two-cover of W+s in the no-component-drop branch has exactly one selected s|W transition. The unique-transition normal form in R560 says that one rail is one W-block with s attached at one end and the other rail is the second pure W-block. Thus s is a literal rail endpoint.

Deleting that terminal s leaves a literal exact two-cover F_s of W. Therefore each singleton cube fiber has the sharp alternative:

  COMMON-W COMPONENT DROP,

or

  ENDPOINT ATTACHMENT s -> F_s.                     (BCB.4)

No source-currentness beyond the actual chosen T_s is asserted.

### 5. The pair and top fibers have finite block alphabets
For |J|=2, (BCB.3) leaves exactly

  (p_J,tau_J)=(1,1) or (0,2).

For J=P,

  p_P+tau_P=3,

recovering the familiar three-cell arithmetic without assuming any special Hamilton order on K. Thus the block-count reduction is order-uniform across the entire Boolean cube.

### 6. Three singleton fibers reduce to one common endpoint trident modulo exact-cover disagreement
Suppose the endpoint-attachment branch of (BCB.4) is chosen for s=p,q,r, and trim the terminal spoke from each chosen T_s. This gives three exact two-covers

  F_p, F_q, F_r

of the same physical core W.

Compare them using accepted R471. If two rail-support partitions differ, the R410/R471 balanced-pair output occurs. If the support partitions agree but a literal Hamilton rail order differs, R435 gives the corresponding reversal, reverse-trimer, or proper-cycle geometry. Outside those explicit disagreement outputs the three trimmed covers are literally one common two-cover

  F=A|B

up to rail exchange.

In that common-base branch, p,q,r are three literal singleton endpoint attachments to the four oriented ends of the same physical two-cover F. This endpoint trident is a finite static object. It is the correct residual object for a full-window source-and-complement exchange theorem.

### 7. Scope
This section does not count R159, R410, or R435 output as extinction. Those are constructive data and still need a direct consumer under the active Astra guidance. It also does not claim that endpoint attachments on different singleton fibers are simultaneously current before the common-base comparison is made. The gain is a coordinate-preserving reduction: every nonempty Boolean fiber is either visibly higher-fragmented over the common W or has exactly two W-blocks with the exact conservation law (BCB.3), and every quiet singleton fiber is a literal endpoint attachment. No special P5 order, PAYABLE-FOUR payment, R24, or R5 is used.
